items.question: Do I need to connect my Web3 wallet to read guides?
items.answer: No. NodeDrops is an educational platform and strictly enforces a zero-wallet policy for browsing documentation and using tools.

items.question: Are airdrops guaranteed for testnet node runners?
items.answer: No. Testnet campaigns are independent and subject to project foundations. We label reward statuses transparently as Confirmed, Potential, None, or Unknown.

items.question: Can I run multiple blockchain nodes on one VPS?
items.answer: It depends on storage IOPS and RAM. CPU and NVMe disk throughput are typically the primary bottlenecks when pairing execution and consensus daemons.

guides.title: How to Run an Ethereum Sepolia Full Node with Geth and Lighthouse
guides.excerpt: Complete step-by-step technical guide to deploying a paired Execution Client (Go-Ethereum) and Consensus Client (Lighthouse) on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.
guides.content:
Running a paired Ethereum testnet node allows you to verify blocks locally, broadcast transactions without third-party rate limits, and test smart contract deployments in a production-identical PoS environment.

### Prerequisites
- An Ubuntu 24.04 / 22.04 LTS server with root or sudo access.
- Static public IPv4 address.
- Configured firewall (UFW) with required P2P ports open.

### Architecture Overview
Ethereum requires two software daemons running concurrently and communicating via the JWT-authenticated Engine API on port 8551:
1. **Execution Client (Geth):** Manages the state trie, processes EVM bytecode, and handles transaction gossip.
2. **Consensus Client (Lighthouse):** Follows the Proof of Stake beacon chain and tracks block attestations.

steps.title: System Preparation and Firewall Configuration
steps.explanation: Update existing packages, install essential tools, and configure UFW to protect RPC interfaces while exposing P2P ports.
steps.command:
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y curl ufw git jq
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw default allow outgoing
sudo ufw allow 22/tcp comment "SSH"
sudo ufw allow 30303/tcp comment "Geth P2P TCP"
sudo ufw allow 30303/udp comment "Geth P2P UDP"
sudo ufw allow 9000/tcp comment "Lighthouse P2P TCP"
sudo ufw allow 9000/udp comment "Lighthouse P2P UDP"
sudo ufw enable
steps.expectedOutput: Firewall is active and enabled on system startup
steps.warning: Never expose port 8545 (HTTP RPC) or 8551 (Engine API) to 0.0.0.0. Keep them bound strictly to 127.0.0.1.
steps.verificationInstructions: Run 'sudo ufw status verbose' and confirm that only ports 22, 30303, and 9000 are open to incoming traffic.

steps.title: Generate Engine API Authentication Secret (JWT)
steps.explanation: Generate a cryptographically secure 32-byte hexadecimal secret shared between Geth and Lighthouse to secure inter-process communication.
steps.command:
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/ethereum/jwt
openssl rand -hex 32 | sudo tee /var/lib/ethereum/jwt/jwt.hex > /dev/null
sudo chmod 600 /var/lib/ethereum/jwt/jwt.hex
steps.warning: If permissions are wrong, Geth or Lighthouse will refuse to start for security.
steps.verificationInstructions: Verify file presence and permissions with 'ls -la /var/lib/ethereum/jwt/jwt.hex'. It should show -rw-------.

steps.title: Install and Configure Go-Ethereum (Geth)
steps.explanation: Install Geth using the official Ethereum PPA and create a dedicated systemd service.
steps.command:
sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:ethereum/ethereum
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y geth

steps.title: Launch Sepolia Sync and Verify Logs
steps.explanation: Start the execution client on the Sepolia network and inspect peer discovery logs.
steps.expectedOutput:
INFO [03-18|10:14:02.124] Starting Geth on Sepolia testnet...
INFO [03-18|10:14:04.912] Looking for peers...
steps.verificationInstructions: Look for 'Looking for peers' followed by peer connection notifications and block header sync.

guides.title: Setting Up a Celestia Light Node on Mocha Testnet
guides.excerpt: Deploy and run a lightweight Data Availability Sampling (DAS) node for Celestia with low hardware overhead.
guides.content:
Celestia light nodes ensure data availability by conducting Data Availability Sampling over the libp2p network without storing the entire chain state.

### Why Run a Light Node?
- Verify block data availability directly from your terminal.
- Support network decentralization with under 2GB RAM.
- No validator stake or high-bandwidth requirement needed.

steps.title: Install Celestia Node Binary
steps.explanation: Download the prebuilt celestia node binary from the official Celestia GitHub release.
steps.command:
cd $HOME
wget https://github.com/celestiaorg/celestia-node/releases/download/v0.18.2/celestia-node_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz
tar -xvf celestia-node_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz
sudo mv celestia /usr/local/bin/
steps.verificationInstructions: Execute 'celestia version' to confirm version 0.18.2 or later is installed.

steps.title: Initialize the Light Node Store
steps.explanation: Initialize the light node configuration directory for the Mocha testnet network.

steps.title: Start Light Node and Sample Blocks
steps.explanation: Start the light node service and connect to trusted core gRPC endpoints.
steps.expectedOutput: INFO header/sync: sync complete to head block
steps.verificationInstructions: Observe the log messages showing sampled headers and sampling success rates.

guides.excerpt: Step-by-step instructions for running a Berachain bArtio node using Docker and systemd.
guides.content: Berachain uses the Polaris EVM modular execution environment on top of CometBFT consensus. This guide covers deploying a full synchronized node on the bArtio testnet.

steps.title: Hardware Benchmark Verification
steps.explanation: Verify your server meets the 8-core CPU and high NVMe IOPS threshold before initializing the state database.
steps.verificationInstructions: Ensure available disk space on root mount is at least 800GB.

guides.title: Linux Security Hardening for Blockchain Node Operators
guides.excerpt: Essential security configurations: SSH key authentication, disabling root login, Fail2ban, UFW, automatic updates, and systemd sandboxing.
guides.content:
Security is the foremost responsibility of any node operator or validator. An insecure node can lead to unauthorized private key extraction, slashing, or distributed denial-of-service vulnerability.

### Core Hardening Pillars
1. **Disable Password Authentication:** Use modern Ed25519 SSH keys.
2. **Restrict Port Exposure:** RPC ports (e.g. 8545, 26657) must never be open to the public internet without mutual TLS or VPN.
3. **Fail2ban:** Block brute-force authentication scans.

steps.title: Create Dedicated Non-Root Service User
steps.explanation: Run node software under an unprivileged system user without sudo permissions.
steps.command:
sudo useradd -r -s /usr/sbin/nologin -d /var/lib/node nodeoperator
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/node
sudo chown -R nodeoperator:nodeoperator /var/lib/node

guides.title: Deploying a Babylon Bitcoin Staking Testnet Node
guides.excerpt: Run a Babylon testnet node to participate in Bitcoin timestamping protocol verification with CometBFT consensus.
guides.content: Babylon brings Bitcoin-level security to Proof-of-Stake blockchains through innovative Bitcoin timestamping protocols. This guide walks through initializing the babylond daemon and synchronizing with the testnet.

steps.title: Download and Install babylond Binary
steps.explanation: Retrieve the verified release binary from the Babylon GitHub repository and add it to your PATH.
steps.command:
wget https://github.com/babylonchain/babylon/releases/download/v0.8.5/babylond_0.8.5_linux_amd64.tar.gz
tar -xvf babylond_0.8.5_linux_amd64.tar.gz
sudo mv babylond /usr/local/bin/
babylond version

steps.title: Initialize Node and Configure Moniker
steps.explanation: Initialize node keys and genesis state for the bbn-test-3 network.
steps.verificationInstructions: Verify sha256 checksum of genesis.json matches official release.

guides.title: Solana Testnet Validator Node Deployment & Performance Tuning
guides.excerpt: Enterprise Linux setup for Solana validator nodes: sysctl kernel tuning, RAM disk account storage, and gossip verification.
guides.content: Solana requires extraordinary system throughput and low latency. This guide covers the critical Linux kernel tuning, file descriptor limits, and CPU governor modes essential for running a validator without falling behind slot production.

steps.title: Kernel and Network Sysctl Optimization
steps.explanation: Configure Linux socket buffer sizes and memory maps to support Solana's high network packet velocity.
steps.command:
sudo bash -c "cat > /etc/sysctl.d/21-solana-validator.conf <<EOF
net.core.rmem_max=134217728
net.core.rmem_default=134217728
net.core.wmem_max=134217728
net.core.wmem_default=134217728
vm.max_map_count=1000000
fs.file-max=1000000
EOF"
sudo sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/21-solana-validator.conf
steps.verificationInstructions: Verify sysctl settings applied without errors.

commandTemplates.name: Geth Sepolia Systemd Service Unit
commandTemplates.templateContent:
[Unit]
Description=Go Ethereum Client - Sepolia
After=network.target
Wants=network.target

[Service]
User=ethereum
Group=ethereum
Type=simple
Restart=always
RestartSec=5
ExecStart=/usr/bin/geth \
  --sepolia \
  --datadir /var/lib/ethereum/geth \
  --authrpc.jwtsecret /var/lib/ethereum/jwt/jwt.hex \
  --authrpc.addr 127.0.0.1 \
  --authrpc.port 8551 \
  --http \
  --http.addr 127.0.0.1 \
  --http.port 8545 \
  --http.api eth,net,web3 \
  --metrics \
  --metrics.addr 127.0.0.1

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
commandTemplates.validationNotes: Production tested. Ensures HTTP and Engine RPC are bound only to localhost loopback.

commandTemplates.name: Celestia Mocha Light Node Docker Compose
commandTemplates.templateContent:
services:
  celestia-light:
    image: ghcr.io/celestiaorg/celestia-node:v0.18.2
    container_name: celestia-light-mocha
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: celestia light start --core.ip rpc-mocha.celestia.net --p2p.network mocha
    volumes:
      - celestia_data:/home/celestia/.celestia-light-mocha-4
    ports:
      - "2121:2121"
    environment:
      - NODE_TYPE=light
      - P2P_NETWORK=mocha

volumes:
  celestia_data:
commandTemplates.validationNotes: Uses official Celestia container repository with named volume persistence.

troubleshooting.title: Resolving Node Disk Space Exhaustion & Safe Pruning
troubleshooting.symptoms: Node service stops abruptly; error message 'no space left on device'; state database corruption warning in system logs.
troubleshooting.likelyCauses: Ancient block headers, debug traces, or state trie accumulation filled available disk volume.
troubleshooting.correctiveSteps:
1. Stop the node daemon cleanly using systemctl:
   sudo systemctl stop geth
2. Check if client supports online or offline snapshot pruning.
3. For Geth: execute prune-state:
   geth snapshot prune-state --datadir /var/lib/ethereum/geth
4. Restart service and monitor free disk:
   sudo systemctl start geth && df -h
troubleshooting.riskWarnings: NEVER run 'rm -rf' on client data directories while the process is running. State pruning can take 3 to 10 hours; do not interrupt it.
troubleshooting.verificationInstructions: Run 'df -h' and confirm at least 20% free space on the data volume. Verify node resumes sync from previous block height.

troubleshooting.title: Zero Peers Connected: P2P Discovery and Port Forwarding Failure
troubleshooting.symptoms: Node boots but peer count stays at 0; block height does not advance; 'no suitable peers found' in logs.
troubleshooting.likelyCauses: Inbound P2P ports blocked by VPS firewall, missing bootnodes in config, or clock skew on the host machine.
troubleshooting.diagnosticCommands:
sudo ufw status
timedatectl status
curl -s http://localhost:8545 -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"net_peerCount","params":[],"id":1}'
troubleshooting.correctiveSteps:
1. Verify system clock is synchronized via NTP:
   sudo timedatectl set-ntp true
2. Confirm P2P ports (e.g. 30303 or 26656) allow both TCP and UDP:
   sudo ufw allow 30303/tcp && sudo ufw allow 30303/udp
3. Append official static bootnodes to client configuration file.
4. Restart node service and tail logs for peer handshakes.
troubleshooting.riskWarnings: Ensure you do not accidentally open RPC ports (8545, 8551, 26657) while modifying firewall rules.
troubleshooting.verificationInstructions: Query peer count via RPC or CLI and verify count is > 10 within 3 minutes.

troubleshooting.title: Consensus & Execution Engine API JWT Authentication Failure
troubleshooting.symptoms: Lighthouse/Prysm logs: 'HTTP error 401 Unauthorized from execution client' or 'Invalid JWT token'.
troubleshooting.likelyCauses: Geth and Lighthouse point to different JWT secret files, or file permissions prevent one daemon from reading it.
troubleshooting.correctiveSteps:
1. Ensure both clients point to the EXACT same path: /var/lib/ethereum/jwt/jwt.hex.
2. Grant read permissions to both service accounts or shared group:
   sudo chmod 644 /var/lib/ethereum/jwt/jwt.hex
3. Restart both services:
   sudo systemctl restart geth && sudo systemctl restart lighthouse-beacon
troubleshooting.riskWarnings: Do not leave JWT directory world-writable (777).
troubleshooting.verificationInstructions: Inspect consensus client logs with 'journalctl -u lighthouse-beacon -f' and verify 'Engine API connection established'.
